items.title: Five motorcycles seized after man repeatedly caught for extreme modifications
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The actions of a man who spent up to RM25,000 to extremely modify five motorcycles backfired when all the vehicles were confiscated by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) after he was detained five times since last year. JPJ Senior Director of Enforcement Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said the fifth motorcycle belonging to the self-employed man was detained during JPJ’s Op Ekstrem around the capital recently for offences involving the modification of engine structures, braking systems, and the use of components not complying with safety specifications. He said that throughout Op Ekstrem conducted on August 8 and 9, a total of 443 motorcycles were inspected, with 336 of them acted against and 140 motorcycles confiscated.

items.title: Muhyiddin urges govt to complete forensic audit of Tabung Haji funds within a year
items.summary: The former prime minister said the move was important following weaknesses in governance and transparency in the management of TH funds, as revealed in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution. “Anyone responsible for causing losses to TH funds, whether through fraud, abuse of power or negligence, must be brought to justice,” he said during the debate on the TH RCI report at the Special Dewan Rakyat Sitting today. Meanwhile, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (MUDA-Muar) urged the government to establish a Multi-Agency Task Force to investigate 14 problematic TH investments identified in the RCI report.

items.title: DAP leader slams opposition boycott of Tabung Haji RCI debate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: DAP central executive committee member Senator Sheikh Umar Bagharib Ali has criticised opposition members of parliament, who walked out of the Dewan Rakyat, today. The walkout came during the debate on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Lembaga Tabung Haji. The Johor DAP deputy chairman said the move was regrettable as the debate provided MPs an opportunity to scrutinise the RCI findings and raise issues concerning Tabung Haji depositors.

items.title: Millions of burnt books show how 'war of endurance' is hurting Ukraine
items.summary: VIKTOR Kruhlov, director of Ranok, one of Ukraine's largest children's publishers, struggled to hold back tears as he watched pile after pile of his books turn to ash. "It's a terrible sight to see books burning," he said. A Russian drone strike on Ranok's warehouse in the northeastern city of Kharkiv on Aug 1 destroyed about eight million books, the biggest blow yet to Ukraine's publishing industry during the four-year-old war.

items.title: Tune Talk offers local users free E-Roaming in popular travel destinations
items.summary: Tune Talk has expanded its Epik+ 50 mobile plan by introducing complimentary E-Roaming in selected destinations, allowing subscribers to stay connected overseas without incurring additional roaming charges. AVAILABLE IN 13 DESTINATIONS According to Tourism Malaysia's outbound travel data , Indonesia (35.2 per cent), Thailand (30.7 per cent), Singapore (18.4 per cent) and Japan (14.3 per cent) rank among the top planned international holiday destinations for Malaysians. These destinations are also among the 13 countries covered under Tune Talk's complimentary E-Roaming offering.

items.title: Study finds common plastics can biodegrade within two years
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Common plastics that can persist in the environment for hundreds of years can be fully broken down by naturally occurring microbes within two years, according to a study by Malaysia's Standards and Industrial Research Institute (Sirim), Imperial College London and biotechnology firm Polymateria. Sirim carried out the biodegradation testing for the study, which also substantiates its national Ecolabel, SIRIM ECO 098, published in 2023 based on the UK standard BSI PAS 9017. Researchers found that polyethylene and polypropylene — the two most widely used plastic packaging materials, found in products such as cups, straws, plastic bags, films, face masks and wipes — can fully biodegrade in nature when incorporating the technology.

items.title: Police question KLIA staff in pilot drug probe, insider link still unclear
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Police have questioned a Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) staff member as part of investigations into the Malaysian pilot arrested with drugs in Jakarta, but it is still too early to determine whether there was any insider involvement. Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan confirmed that investigators had recorded his statement. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Bukit Aman sends narcotics team to Jakarta to question Malaysian pilot held with 26kg ecstasy
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 11 — A team of officers from the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department has arrived in Indonesia to question a Malaysian pilot arrested with drugs at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport last month. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Commissioner Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the team of four arrived earlier today and has been given two days, August 12 to 13, to interrogate the suspect. Hussein said investigators were tracing the alleged syndicate members but faced some difficulties because the phone numbers used for communication were registered under false or inaccurate identities.

items.title: Economic losses from natural disasters fall to US$100bil in first half of 2026: Swiss Re
items.summary: ZURICH: Economic losses from natural catastrophes worldwide are estimated to have reached US$100 billion in the first half of this year, reinsurance group Swiss Re said Tuesday, a sharp decline from the period last year. Despite severe storms in the United States and the deadly earthquakes that struck Venezuela in June, the losses were well below the US$152 billion recorded in the first half of 2025, the group said in its latest report. "A less costly first half of the year does not mean the risk has gone away," said Balz Grollimund, the group's director of Catastrophe Perils.

items.title: Police detain eight over suspected murder of man at Kuala Langat oil palm plantation
items.summary: KUALA LANGAT, Aug 11 — Police are investigating the death of a man believed to have been murdered at an oil palm plantation in Sungai Kelambu, Banting here last Sunday. Kuala Langat District Police chief Supt Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi, in a statement, said eight individuals had been arrested to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code. Akmalrizal also urged members of the public with information to go to the nearest police station or contact the Kuala Langat District Police Headquarters Operations Room at 03-3187 2222.

items.title: [UPDATED] Only 6pct of drugs got through KLIA in first seven months - Hussein
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Drugs that slipped through Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) before being intercepted overseas accounted for only about six per cent of the total drugs seized by police at the airport in the first seven months of this year. "Of the 51 people arrested at KLIA, 36, or 70.6 per cent, were men, while 15, or 29.4 per cent, were women. "Six per cent.

items.title: Five houses damaged in Kampung Tanah Liat fire
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Five houses were damaged, including two that were extensively destroyed, in a fire along Jalan Paya, Kampung Tanah Liat, today. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 12.32pm. He said the fire involved two two-storey and three single-storey houses, each measuring about 50 by 60 feet.

items.title: Pilot drug case: Syndicate phone linked to false identity
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A telephone number used by a drug syndicate to communicate with the Malaysian pilot arrested in Indonesia is believed to have been falsely registered. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said this had made identifying the person behind the number more complicated. He said investigators could not simply trace the registered owner of a telephone number and assume that person was the actual user.

items.title: Rhine water levels fall to new lows, some ship sailings halted
items.summary: HAMBURG: The river Rhine in Germany has fallen to new lows in a continued heatwave, the country's inland navigation agency said on Tuesday, with cargo vessel owners often stopping sailings on southern river sections. Inland navigation agency WSV said the navigable water depth at the chokepoint of Kaub near Koblenz was 15 cm on Tuesday, below the previous lowest recorded level of 25 cm in 2018. "Commercial sailings through Kaub have basically stopped, it is no longer possible to book cargo shipments on the Rhine past Kaub today," one commodity trader said.

items.title: IGP: Police officers must keep evolving as security landscape grows more dynamic
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail has urged all police officers to think critically, act swiftly and remain relevant amid changing times to meet the challenges of an increasingly dynamic policing landscape. “Promotion is not the pinnacle of a career, but rather the starting point of far greater and more challenging responsibilities,” he said at the Police Senior Officers’ Rank Insignia and Honorary Rank Insignia Presentation Ceremony at the Senior Police Officers’ Mess, Bukit Aman here today. A total of 29 senior police officers were honoured at the ceremony for their promotions to the ranks of Commissioner of Police (CP), Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Senior Assistant Commissioner (SAC) and Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP).

items.title: Johor police bust drug syndicate supplying local market, seize RM8.49m worth of drugs
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 11 — Johor police have busted a drug trafficking syndicate following the arrest of two men and the seizure of various types of drugs worth RM8.49 million in two separate raids in the Seri Alam area here on Wednesday (Aug 5). Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the raids were conducted at an apartment in Masai and a terrace house in Taman Ehsan Jaya at about 10.30 am. “Upon inspecting the apartment, we seized 132,600 Erimin 5 pills, 53,000 ecstasy pills, 290 packets of ecstasy powder, 13 packets of ketamine and two packets of Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) powder, weighing 96.76 kg in total,” he told a press conference at the Johor Police Headquarters here today.

items.title: [UPDATED] Four NCID officers arrive in Jakarta, get two-day access to M'sian pilot
items.summary: "Four NCID officers arrived in Jakarta this morning. Hussein said the officers would use the interviews to compare information obtained from investigations in Malaysia with the pilot's account. Hussein said the team would also meet three Malaysian women from Kota Kinabalu who were detained in Jakarta in a separate drug case.

items.title: PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim says lawyers handling Anwar’s defamation suit
items.summary: KOTA BARU, Aug 11 — PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said he would leave it to his lawyers to respond to the defamation suit filed against him by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The Kubang Kerian MP said the remarks at the centre of the suit were general in nature and had also been raised by other parties and sources, the New Straits Times reported. Anwar’s lawyer, Datuk Sankara Nair, said the statements were false and defamatory of the Prime Minister.

items.title: [UPDATED] 'KLIA too hot': International drug syndicates turning to other airports
items.summary: This shift was observed during Op Lejogaster, where police uncovered an international syndicate which planned to move cannabis buds out of the country through Penang International Airport in Bayan Lepas. Police seized RM21.62 million worth of cannabis buds through this latest operations. Hussein said investigations under Op Lejogaster showed how the syndicate had made use of locations near airports as part of its trafficking operation.

items.title: Johor Baru-Singapore RTS LINK set to lift JB property demand, but Malaysians may drive growth
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link is expected to lift property demand in central Johor Baru, particularly around Bukit Chagar. "The RTS is likely to increase demand for homes in central Johor Baru, especially around Bukit Chagar. However, Nasser said the RTS property premium would depend largely on connectivity beyond Bukit Chagar.

items.title: Hong Kong deepens Malaysia's and Asean trade ties with a new Kuala Lumpur office
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Kong is stepping up economic and trade ties with Malaysia and the wider Asean region through a newly established Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office (HKETO) in Kuala Lumpur. Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Commerce and Economic Development secretary Algernon Yau said the office would strengthen government-to-government and business-to-business links. Together with the Hong Kong Trade Development Council, Invest Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Tourism Board, the Kuala Lumpur ETO will steer ahead," he said.

items.title: Four-month-old baby girl’s death in Johor probed as murder, investigation papers sent to prosecution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Police have reclassified the death of a four-month-old baby girl in Taman Sri Saujana in Johor Bahru as murder, with the investigation papers referred to the Johor prosecution office for further action. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the investigation was initially conducted under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 for neglect resulting in the baby’s death, before being reclassified under Section 302 of the Penal Code following a post-mortem. He said the completed investigation papers were referred to the Johor prosecution office yesterday, while police had received instructions to charge the baby’s step-grandmother under Section 302 at the Kota Tinggi Magistrates’ Court tomorrow.

items.title: Ebola deaths surpass 2,000 in Democratic Republic of Congo
items.summary: DAKAR: Democratic Republic of Congo said on Tuesday that confirmed Ebola deaths had reached 2,011, the latest grim milestone in what health officials have described as the fastest-spreading outbreak on record. The latest data from Congo's public health institute, seen by Reuters, also reported 4,381 confirmed cases across five provinces. It took nearly five months from the declaration of that outbreak to hit 1,000 deaths, whereas Congo's current outbreak has hit 2,000 deaths in less than three months.

items.title: Israeli soldiers, settlers use grenades and physical assaults against Palestinian journalists
items.summary: RAMALLAH: The Palestinian Journalists Syndicate said it documented 108 attacks and other violations against Palestinian journalists and media workers by Israeli occupation forces and settlers during July, Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA) reported. In its monthly report, the syndicate's Freedoms Committee said the violations included detentions, interrogations, physical assaults, obstruction of media coverage, raids and attacks involving tear gas and stun grenades. The committee also recorded 11 attacks by Israeli settlers against journalists and media crews in the West Bank.

items.title: Sarawak orders schools to halt outdoor activities amid unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Schools in Sarawak have been ordered to immediately halt all outdoor activities involving pupils in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100. Sarawak Education Department director Omar Mahli said district education offices and educational institutions under the department had been reminded to prioritise the welfare, health and safety of pupils amid hot weather and haze, Utusan Malaysia reported today. “For areas recording API readings above 100, all outdoor activities involving pupils must be stopped,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Malaysia's low costs, talent draw investors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's competitive labour costs, low land prices and strong human resources have made the country investor-friendly, said Hong Kong-listed Far East Consortium International Ltd. Its chairman and chief executive officer Tan Sri David Chiu said Malaysia's cultural similarities with Hong Kong also make it easier for Malaysian professionals to manage businesses and operations there. "If you have a team in Malaysia (and) you want to send them to Hong Kong to run your business there, it is not at all difficult because of the similar culture (between Malaysia and Hong Kong)," he said during a plenary session at the Think Business, Think Hong Kong symposium here today. Today's symposium marked the Hong Kong Trade Development Council's (HKTDC) flagship overseas promotion in Kuala Lumpur, offering Malaysian business leaders direct access to government officials, investors, founders, innovators and professional service providers.

items.title: Woman, 78, believed killed in crocodile attack while collecting river snails in Batu Niah
items.summary: The victim has been identified as Sambai Anggah. According to the Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba), Sambai and her 31-year-old daughter were searching for snails around a tributary connected to Sungai Suai when the incident occurred. Her daughter, who was in the river about one metre away, witnessed the crocodile snare Sambai from the boat.

items.title: Pas deputy president Tuan Ibrahim leaves Anwar defamation suit to lawyers
items.summary: KOTA BARU: PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said he had left the matter concerning the defamation suit filed against him by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to his lawyers. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has filed a defamation suit against Tuan Ibrahim over remarks allegedly made during a political speech in June. Anwar's lawyer, Datuk Sankara Nair, said the suit was filed at the High Court on Monday.

items.title: Johor sets up special team to probe claims of Singapore waste dumped in Pontian
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 11 — The Johor government has set up a special team to investigate claims that construction waste from Singapore is illegally dumped in Pontian. Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the team was formed with an integrated approach to enable a comprehensive investigation into the allegations. Mohd Jafni was responding to claims that construction waste from Singapore had entered Johor and was dumped in Pontian.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI: MPs call for transparent probe, accountability to protect depositors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Members of Parliament across the political divide today called for independent and transparent investigations into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) after it was tabled in Parliament. Government backbenchers, led by Sekijang MP Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa, called on the government to clarify the involvement of TH’s leadership between 2014 and 2020 in negotiations over investments and allegations surrounding the matter. Dr Zaliha also called on the government to publish a complete report on the progress of the 25 recommendations made by the RCI to restore depositors’ confidence in TH.

items.title: Man appealing for shorter sentence gets maximum 30 years for baby daughter's death
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A man who appealed for a shorter jail term for causing his 2-month-old daughter's death had his sentence increased to 30 years by the Court of Appeal today. Justice Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz, who delivered the decision of a three-member bench, said the court had discretionary power under Section 60 of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964 to enhance the sentence despite the lack of a prosecution cross-appeal. Hayatul said the 16-year prison sentence imposed by the Shah Alam High Court did not reflect the seriousness of the offence and the violence involved.

items.title: RM8.49mil drug haul seized from apartment in Masai, two arrested
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police busted a drug distribution syndicate after seizing 96.76kg of various drugs worth RM8.49 million from an apartment in Persiaran Senibong, Masai, which had allegedly been rented as a storage facility. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the raid on Aug 5 led to the arrest of the two men suspected to be involved in the syndicate. "Checks uncovered 132,600 Ermin 5 pills, 53,000 ecstasy pills, 290 packets of suspected ecstasy powder, 13 packets of suspected ketamine and packets of suspected MDMA powder," he told a press conference at the Johor police headquarters here today.

items.title: Human oversight must remain central as newsrooms embrace AI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Artificial intelligence (AI) can make newsrooms more productive, but it cannot replace the editorial judgement and accountability that underpin credible journalism, media practitioners said. Former Media Prima Bhd news and editorial operations executive director and New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd chief executive officer Mustapha Kamil said the extent to which AI would reshape journalism remains an open question. "AI is a tool.

items.title: Appeal backfires as man’s sentence for causing two-month-old daughter’s death raised to 30 years
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 11 — A man who appealed for a shorter prison sentence for causing the death of his two-month-old daughter instead had his sentence increased to the maximum 30 years by the Court of Appeal here today. Justice Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz, who delivered the decision of a three-member bench, said although the prosecution had not cross-appealed against the sentence, the court had the discretionary power under Section 60 of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964 (CJA) to enhance Muhammad Daniel Iman Mohd Sharif’s sentence. Justice Hayatul said the 16-year prison sentence imposed by the Shah Alam High Court did not reflect the seriousness of the offence and the violence involved.

items.title: US$620mil returned to sender, not Najib's account, court hears
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The US$620 million returned by former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to its sender in 2013 was not transferred back into his bank account, the High Court heard today. Offshore asset recovery expert Angela Barkhouse, the third witness for 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), agreed with Najib's lawyer Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah that the money was returned to Tanore Finance Corp, which he identified as the sender. Asked whether she knew why Najib returned the US$620 million, Barkhouse said: "I do not know."

items.title: Pahang Pas: Door open to Umno cooperation, or election clash
items.summary: KUANTAN: Pahang Pas is open to political cooperation with Umno under the 'penyatuan ummah' (Muslim unity) concept ahead of the 16th General Election. Pahang Pas commissioner Datuk Rosli Abdul Jabar said no discussions had been held with Barisan Nasional or Umno so far, but the party was ready to sit down for talks. Last week, Pahang Pas deputy commissioner Datuk Andansura Rabu said the ongoing Perikatan Nasional Jelajah Teraju Pahang campaign, led by Pas, would proceed as scheduled.

items.title: Man jailed two years for punching wife, attempting to murder her with car
items.summary: KANGAR, Aug 12 — A man was sentenced to two years in prison by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to injuring and attempting to murder his wife in September last year. Judge Sharifah Norazlita Syed Salim Idid sentenced Mohd Hasmi Mohd Salleh, 39, to one year in prison for intentionally causing hurt to his wife and two years for attempting to murder her, with the sentences to run concurrently from the date of his arrest on Sept 21, 2025. On the first charge, Mohd Hasmi was accused of punching his wife, Norzuraida Don Khodet, on her right arm, causing bruising.

items.title: No enemies, debts: Family suspects mistaken identity in Kepong attack
items.summary: The victim's daughter, Joyce Yap, said the family had no known enemies or outstanding debts and could not understand why her mother was targeted. Yap said the absence of any previous threats or disputes led the family to suspect the attacker may have mistaken her mother for someone else. She said her mother remained in critical condition and was receiving intensive care in the intensive care unit of a hospital.

items.title: Tabung Haji Act amendments to introduce tougher financial reporting rules, penalties
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Zulkifli Hasan said the changes were intended to prevent a recurrence of the issues highlighted by the RCI in its report on TH management and operations from 2014 to 2020. “All relevant RCI recommendations have been reviewed for inclusion in the proposed amendments to the TH Act, including the suitability of a Securities Commission oversight and supervisory framework for TH’s fund management and investments,” he said when presenting his ministerial briefing on the RCI report at the special Dewan Rakyat sitting today. TH would remain a single, intact entity,” he said.

items.title: Muhyiddin calls for Tabung Haji forensic audit to be completed within a year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin has called on the government to complete a comprehensive and independent forensic audit of Tabung Haji's management within a year. "Given the complex governance weaknesses and leakages in Tabung Haji's fund management, a comprehensive and continuous forensic audit must be carried out immediately and completed within one year. "Anyone responsible for causing losses to Tabung Haji's funds, whether through fraud, abuse of power or negligence, must be brought to justice," Muhyiddin said while debating the RCI report in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Johor orders Kempas scrap metal recycling premise to shut down over air pollution risk
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 11 — The Johor government has ordered an illegal scrap metal recycling premise in Kampung Maju Jaya, Kempas, here, to shut down immediately following claims of air pollution. The premise is also located near an underground gas pipeline owned by Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), raising safety concerns for more than 10,000 residents in four nearby villages. Also present were Johor Bahru Mayor Datuk Mohd Haffiz Ahmad, Johor Bahru North police chief Assistant Commissioner Radin Ramlan Ramdin Taha and Johor Solid Waste Management Corporation (SWCorp) director Zainal Fitri Ahmad.

items.title: MP: TH leadership sackings in 2021 must be explained
items.summary: Syerleena Abdul Rashid (PH-Bukit Bendera) said the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) found that the move had affected the institution's reform process. Syerleena said the RCI found that TH chief executive officer Datuk Nik Mohd Hasyudeen Yusoff and chairman Tan Sri Md Nor Md Yusof had delivered and were working to improve the institution before their contracts were terminated. This is a finding of the RCI," she said during a special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat to debate the RCI report on TH today.

items.title: Dogs top animal abuse, neglect cases in Malaysia, says group
items.summary: Malaysian Animal Association president Associate Professor Arie Dwi Andika said records obtained from authorities showed dogs accounted for the highest number of reported cases, followed by cats, horses and cattle. "Many dogs are abused, beaten and poisoned. In 2023, 38,833 complaints involving dogs, including nuisance cases reported to local authorities, were recorded," he said.

items.title: Civil society groups, PKR members demand action on TH RCI findings
items.summary: The group gathered outside Parliament today and handed over the memorandums to representatives from the Prime Minister's Office and the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs). The first memorandum, addressed to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, outlined six demands focused on accountability, governance reform and transparency. The second memorandum, addressed to Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, called for the RCI findings to be assessed from the perspective of Islamic law and maqasid syariah, given TH's role in managing the savings of millions of Muslims seeking to perform the haj.

items.title: Are e-wallets better than cards and cash in Malaysia?
items.summary: E-WALLETS are often more convenient than cards or cash for everyday payments in Malaysia, particularly at hawker stalls, cafés, convenience stores and small retailers. Consumers can also make QR payments through banking applications such as MAE by Maybank and CIMB OCTO. Many of these services support DuitNow QR, Malaysia's national QR payment standard.

items.title: Police probe syndicate link after Malaysian held with cannabis in Chennai
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian police have begun investigating the syndicate network linked to a 54-year-old Malaysian detained in India with more than four kilogrammes of hydroponic cannabis. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police would work with India's Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) to obtain further information on the case and trace the network involved. He was detained after Chennai Customs officers inspected his luggage and found about 4kg of hydroponic cannabis concealed inside.

items.title: Selangor seawater desalination plant feasibility study due by December
items.summary: State Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said Central Spectrum (M) Sdn Bhd, in collaboration with Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd (Air Selangor), had appointed a consultant to conduct the study, which was expected to take six months. He said the study was among the state government’s efforts to diversify alternative water supply sources to meet development demands in the area, as well as reduce reliance on existing water treatment plants (LRAs). “Air Selangor projects that water supply demand will increase to 9,653 MLD by 2045.

items.title: Najib returned US$620m after GE13 because he was uncomfortable holding it, High Court told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The High Court here was told today that former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak returned US$620 million out of the US$681 million he received as a purported “Arab donation” because he was uncomfortable keeping such a large amount of money in his bank account. Najib’s lead counsel, Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, said according to his client, the money was returned to the sender, Tanore Finance Corporation, after the 13th General Election (GE13) in 2013. The veteran lawyer said that Najib returned the money to Tanore in the hope that it (Tanore) was part of the Arab donation.

items.title: Make public full report on Tabung Haji RCI reforms, recovery efforts, says Dr Zaliha
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A full report on the implementation of the 25 recommendations of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), along with a report on efforts to recover its losses, should be made public to restore depositors’ confidence, Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa said. The Government Backbenchers Club (BBC) chairman and Sekijang MP said disclosure was important given TH’s role as a key institution for Malaysian Muslims, particularly in managing savings for the haj pilgrimage. The 211-page RCI report was only recently made public.

items.title: Seven-year-old Indonesian boy found drowned after falling into river in Subang Jaya
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A seven-year-old Indonesian boy who fell into a river while playing with friends near Matahari Supermarket in Persiaran Subang Indah in Subang Jaya yesterday was found drowned this morning. The Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) said in a statement that the boy was found at 10.59am by personnel from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station and its Water Rescue Team (PPDA), Astro Awani reported. The search and rescue operation also involved PPDA personnel from the Shah Alam, Port Klang and KLIA fire and rescue stations, as well as personnel from the Puchong station.

items.title: Fix deadline for RCI reports to be tabled in Parliament, says Tuaran MP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The Commissions of Enquiry Act 1950 should be amended to set a deadline for Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) reports to be tabled in Parliament, Tuaran MP Datuk Seri Wilfred Madius Tangau said today. Wilfred said the tabling of RCI reports should not be left solely to the government’s discretion as the purpose of establishing such commissions was to present the truth to the people. “So, the Commissions of Enquiry Act 1950 should be empowered so that tabling of RCI reports in Parliament does not rest solely on discretions (of the government),” Wilfred said during the debate on the Tabung Haji RCI report in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Kelantan opens 63 investigation papers into illegal mining, encroachment
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 11 — A total of 63 investigation papers were opened in connection with encroachment and illegal mining activities in Kelantan from 2025 to June this year. Kelantan Deputy Menteri Besar Datuk Dr Mohamed Fadzli Hassan said the figure resulted from 77 enforcement operations conducted in hotspots involving the Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli and Tanah Merah districts. “The state government, through enforcement agencies, has intensified field action to curb such activities.

items.title: Tabung Haji lost RM145.3m from Putrajaya Perdana investment linked to 1MDB, Dewan Rakyat told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Lembaga Tabung Haji’s (TH) investment in Putrajaya Perdana ultimately dragged it into dealings involving troubled state investment vehicle 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB), resulting in a RM145.3 million loss, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Zulkifli Hasan said the investment was among 14 problematic investments identified in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into TH. “This needs to be given attention: TH invested in Putrajaya Perdana, appointed the then TH chairman as chairman of Putrajaya Perdana, and the company was subsequently embroiled in 1MDB transactions.

items.title: Malaysia’s June unemployment rate stays at 3pc, 517,800 jobless, says Stats Dept
items.summary: The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) said the number of employed persons rose 0.01 per cent to 16.83 million in June 2026 (May 2026: 16.82 million persons), while the number of unemployed persons increased from 513,400 to 517,800, rising by 0.9 per cent month-on-month. “The labour force recorded a marginal month-on-month increase of 0.04 per cent to 17.34 million persons in June 2026 (May 2026: 17.34 million persons). It said the employees’ category comprised 75.0 per cent of the total employed persons, increasing slightly by 0.02 per cent, reaching 12.61 million persons in June 2026 (May 2026: 12.61 million persons), while the number of own-account workers rose marginally by 0.04 per cent to register 3.15 million persons (May 2026: 3.15 million persons).

items.title: Rapid KL confirms sexual harassment allegation on Sri Rampai-Setiawangsa train
items.summary: Online, Rapid KL said that the incident occurred while the train was travelling from Sri Rampai station to Setiawangsa station. Its auxiliary police team subsequently assisted both individuals involved and escorted them to the Setiawangsa police station to lodge a report. “Rapid KL Auxiliary Police provided assistance and escorted both individuals to the Setiawangsa Police Station to lodge a police report,” it said.

items.title: Syed Saddiq calls for forensic audit, multi-agency probe into Tabung Haji investments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A multi-agency task force should be formed and a forensic audit should be launched into Lembaga Tabung Haji’s failed investments, Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman proposed today. Syed Saddiq, Muda’s sole lawmaker in the Parliament, said this was necessary since the Royal Commission of Inquiry’s (RCI) report revealed that Tabung Haji’s failed investments involved a complex network of government-linked investment companies (GLICs). “If not handled properly, it will create (a) tsunami of misgovernance that will result in taxpayers shouldering heavy losses,” Syed Saddiq said during the debate on the Tabung Haji RCI report at the special Parliament sitting today.

items.title: King orders full probe into Tabung Haji RCI findings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has ordered a comprehensive and transparent investigation into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). The Star reported that Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Zulkifli Hasan said the King had instructed that the investigation be conducted without compromise, with no stone left unturned. Zulkifli said the Cabinet had unanimously reviewed the RCI report on July 29 and decided to make it public by tabling and debating it during the special parliamentary sitting.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng says six proposals to help MSMEs rejected by govt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today said six measures he proposed to help micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) cope with rising costs and economic pressures had been rejected by the government. Lim said the measures were necessary to ensure the survival of 1.1 million MSMEs in Malaysia, which he said contributed 38 per cent to the country’s gross domestic product (GDP), accounted for 48 per cent of employment and nearly 13 per cent of total exports. The ministry also said the government had already implemented several measures to support MSMEs affected by rising operating costs, including RM5 billion in guarantees under the Business Financing Guarantee Company (SJPP).

items.title: BNM issued five warning letters to Tabung Haji leadership over asset-liability gap
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) had issued five warning letters to the Tabung Haji (TH) chairman and the Minister of Religious Affairs regarding the gap between TH’s assets and liabilities. “At the time, TH’s position posed a potential systemic risk to the country’s financial stability. Unfortunately, those letters were ignored by TH’s leadership,” he said.

items.title: Two men with combined 52 criminal records nabbed over Jasin KK Mart robbery
items.summary: JASIN, Aug 11 — Police have arrested two men believed to be involved in an armed robbery at a KK Mart convenience store in Taman Maju here on Aug 6. Jasin district police chief Supt Lee Robert said the two suspects, aged 44 and 45, were arrested separately at about 4.30 pm yesterday. He said the first suspect was arrested by the roadside along Jalan PPJ 3 in Jasin town, while the second was arrested in Sagil, Tangkak, Johor.
